raised.claim: Verdicts attached to new issues bypass the row-versus-scope guard.
raised.why_it_breaks: A proposal can declare candidates_count > 0 with no enumerated beer_ids and route a zero-candidate row to that new_issue_key; the planner creates the issue and records the attachment even though the row contradicts its scope.

raised.claim: Adding any enumerated beer ID makes a whole-class where-scope legal.
raised.why_it_breaks: A scope with beer_ids: [1] and where containing only review_class = matcher_bug passes legality; because rowSatisfiesScope combines the cohort and where with OR, every future matcher_bug row also passes, recreating the whole-class dumping ground this guard is intended to reject.

raised.quote:
const body = `${issue.body}\n\n${renderScopeBlock(issue.scope)}`;
        const number = await github.createIssue({ title: issue.title, body, labels: issue.labels });
raised.claim: Model-authored issue prose can override the authoritative structured scope block.
raised.why_it_breaks: If issue.body already contains a valid triage-scope fence, it appears before the rendered block and parseScopeBlock takes that first match on the next run; a broad or unrelated scope in the prose therefore silently replaces the validated structured field.

raised.claim: The saturation guard does not reserve capacity for attachments accepted in the current batch.
raised.why_it_breaks: An issue with 11 post-creation rows can accept all 50 verdicts in a batch because every verdict checks the same unchanged count of 11, allowing the issue to grow to 61 despite MAX_ROWS_PER_ISSUE being 12.

raised.claim: Guard-hit logging is suppressed whenever the model supplies a verdict for every batch row.
raised.why_it_breaks: If all 50 rows receive verdicts but all attachments fail the scope or saturation guard, covered still equals 50 because it counts raw analysis verdicts; no guardHits log is emitted, even if the same rejected proposals recur every day.

raised.claim: One empty probe authorizes an absence verdict even when the other probe finds the beer.
raised.why_it_breaks: For a row with a misspelled brewery, the brewery-only probe can return empty while the name-only probe returns the correct beer; the OR expression still treats absence as proved and preserves not_on_untappd, blocking the paid fallback despite contradictory positive evidence.

raised.claim: Newly degraded matcher_bug verdicts are reported as wontfix in the daily outcome.
raised.why_it_breaks: An unprobed not_on_untappd verdict now enters plan.quiet as matcher_bug, but the job's quiet execution loop increments outcome.wontfix for every class other than not_on_untappd; the database records matcher_bug while the digest incorrectly reports a wontfix decision.

raised.quote:
`SELECT COUNT(*) AS n FROM enrich_failures
        WHERE issue_number = ? AND reviewed_at > ?`,
raised.claim: The post-creation comparison uses incompatible ISO timestamp precisions as plain text.
raised.why_it_breaks: GitHub supplies creation times such as 2026-08-14T06:00:00Z while review writes use toISOString(), such as 2026-08-14T06:00:00.500Z; the latter sorts before the former lexicographically and is excluded even though the review occurred 500 milliseconds after creation.
